overall_summary: Bitcoin is under fresh pressure after slipping below sixty thousand dollars on another large day of spot ETF outflows, while hawkish Fed talk and a strong dollar keep yields elevated. Geopolitical noise from Russia, Ukraine, and the Middle East adds a risk-off overlay. Corporate buying and a helpful CFTC reserve ruling provide some support, but the forward tone stays defensive into Wednesday’s inflation and growth data.
key_points: BTC under $60k on heavy ETF outflows
Hawkish Fed and firm dollar pressure risk assets
MicroStrategy buys more BTC; CFTC ruling constructive
Focus shifts to Wednesday Core PCE and GDP

items.title: Bitcoin hands back Nvidia rally, slips under $60k
items.summary: Bitcoin surged as high as sixty-four thousand five hundred dollars on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang, but quickly gave it all back and traded below sixty thousand on Tuesday. Crypto futures liquidations jumped to about eight hundred forty-four million dollars over twenty-four hours, more than triple the prior day, as the move reversed. Traders should care because the bounce looked like a short squeeze rather than fresh demand, and bitcoin is lagging the stock rebound while macro headwinds and selling pressure remain.
items.impact: Near-term downside pressure and higher volatility as leverage flushes

items.title: Spot bitcoin ETFs see another $570M outflow Monday
items.summary: U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs recorded five hundred sixty-nine point seven million dollars in net outflows on Monday, the fifth straight session of redemptions, led by BlackRock's IBIT at over five hundred million. November outflows have reached roughly four point seven billion dollars, the largest monthly total on record, after nearly one point eight billion left last week. This is structural selling that is overriding short-term equity rallies and removing a key source of demand traders watch closely.
items.impact: Continued institutional selling pressure weighing on price

items.title: Record 11.6 million BTC now underwater after $55k low
items.summary: Bitcoin's weekend drop to about fifty-five thousand dollars pushed a record eleven point six million BTC into unrealized loss, according to Glassnode, while supply in profit fell to eight point five million BTC below the FTX-collapse low. Mid-sized entities holding one hundred to ten thousand BTC kept accumulating even as smaller holders sold. Traders should note this as classic washed-out conditions that have marked bottoms before, though price still needs to hold support for confirmation.
items.impact: Capitulation signal that could support a base if support holds

items.title: Strategy buys another 457 BTC, holdings hit 851k
items.summary: Strategy acquired four hundred fifty-seven bitcoin for about twenty-nine point six million dollars last week at an average near sixty-four thousand nine hundred dollars, lifting total holdings to eight hundred fifty-one thousand three hundred five BTC. The firm spent far more on preferred stock buybacks and raised that program by a billion dollars while still adding to its stack. This keeps the largest corporate holder buying the dip even as its paper losses grow, signaling long-term conviction amid the selloff.
items.impact: Modest positive demand signal from largest corporate buyer

items.title: DOJ moves to forfeit $1.1B from North Korea Binance hack
items.summary: The U.S. Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture action seeking more than one point one billion dollars in frozen USDC stolen in the late-October Binance hack attributed to North Korean actors. Authorities say they have already helped freeze, seize or return over two point nine billion of the more than six billion taken, though billions remain unaccounted for and some funds continue moving. This underscores ongoing recovery efforts and exchange security risks that can affect market confidence and stablecoin flows.
items.impact: Supports industry integrity but limited immediate price catalyst

items.title: CFTC lets BTC and ETH count toward exchange reserves
items.summary: CFTC staff advised that bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins can count toward the twelve-month operating-cost reserves required of regulated derivatives exchanges, swap venues and clearinghouses, subject to haircuts of at least twenty percent for BTC and ETH. Crypto still cannot meet the separate cash or highly liquid securities liquidity minimum. This is a clarity win that lowers a barrier for crypto-friendly venues and signals more mainstream acceptance of major tokens in U.S. derivatives markets.
items.impact: Positive regulatory signal easing costs for crypto derivatives platforms

items.title: Fed's Williams: Inflation Too High, More Hikes Needed
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said Monday that inflation remains too high at around three and a half percent on the PCE measure and the Fed still has work to do to get it sustainably back to two percent. He stressed the economy is strong and resilient with solid growth and a stable labor market, but policy must tighten over time based on data ahead of the December FOMC. Markets now price a near-certain twenty-five basis point hike next month from the three point seven five to four percent range. Crypto traders should care because this locks in higher-for-longer rates and a firmer dollar, which historically pressures risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: Reinforces December hike bets and tighter financial conditions

items.title: US Flash PMI Cools to 54.6 but Still Signals Solid Growth
items.summary: S and P Global flash composite PMI fell to a four-month low of fifty-four point six in November from fifty-five point nine, with services at fifty-four point seven missing forecasts and manufacturing at fifty-four point five. Growth cooled due to capacity constraints, high prices damping orders, and some rate effects, yet hiring stayed strong and the survey still points to about three percent annualized fourth-quarter GDP. Price pressures eased a bit but remain elevated well above the Fed target. Traders watch this as confirmation of resilient but slowing expansion that keeps the Fed hawkish while not crashing demand.
items.impact: Supports soft-landing narrative without derailing hike path

items.title: Dollar Near Multi-Month Highs, Yields Steady Near 4.9%
items.summary: The DXY dollar index hovered near one hundred four point two to one hundred four point five after touching recent highs on Monday, easing only slightly Tuesday as tech rebounded but Fed hike bets stayed firm. The ten-year Treasury yield traded around four point nine percent, down a basis point or so after Williams, with the two-year near four point six six percent. Strong AI-related demand and inflation concerns keep the greenback bid and borrowing costs elevated. For crypto this means continued headwinds from a strong dollar and higher real rates that raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets.
items.impact: Stronger USD and sticky yields pressure risk assets

items.title: Markets Brace for Wednesday Core PCE and GDP Data
items.summary: All eyes turn to Wednesday's release of October core PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, expected around zero point three percent month-over-month and three point two percent year-over-year, alongside the second estimate of third-quarter GDP near three point four percent. Personal income, spending, durable goods and jobless claims also drop at the same time, plus the Beige Book later. A hot print would cement further tightening into December and beyond, while a cool one could ease some pressure. Crypto traders need this because it is the last major inflation checkpoint before the blackout and FOMC, likely driving big volatility in rates, dollar and Bitcoin.
items.impact: Key catalyst that will set December policy expectations

items.title: Chicago Fed Activity Index Slips Below Trend to -0.06
items.summary: The Chicago Fed National Activity Index dropped to minus zero point zero six in October from a revised plus zero point zero five, signaling growth slightly below its long-run trend. Production indicators drove the weakness while employment and sales orders offered some offset; the three-month average also turned mildly negative. This aligns with the softer PMI tone without pointing to recession. It matters for traders as another data point showing the economy is decelerating just enough to keep the Fed data-dependent but not doveish ahead of PCE.
items.impact: Mild cooling signal that does not change hike odds

items.title: Today's Data: Consumer Confidence, Case-Shiller, IP Revision
items.summary: Tuesday's calendar features Conference Board Consumer Confidence for November expected near ninety-two point one to ninety-two point five after October's ninety-one point seven, plus S and P Case-Shiller home prices for September forecast around two point seven percent year-over-year, FHFA house prices, Richmond Fed manufacturing, and the Fed's annual industrial production and capacity utilization revision. These medium-impact releases fill the gap before Wednesday's heavy PCE-GDP day and can nudge yields or the dollar if they surprise. Crypto desks watch for any consumer or housing softness that might temper Fed hawkishness or confirm resilience that supports higher rates.
items.impact: Secondary data that can fine-tune pre-PCE positioning

items.title: Germany warns Russia may launch nuclear satellite soon
items.summary: German intelligence and NATO allies assess that Russia could put a nuclear-armed satellite called Sputnik-S into orbit within 60 days, possibly as early as December. A detonation would risk frying large numbers of satellites including Starlink and create long-lasting radiation belts. Traders should care because this is a genuine black-swan escalation that threatens the space infrastructure modern markets and military ops rely on.
items.impact: elevates global risk premium and satellite-dependent systems fear

items.title: Ukraine sinks Russian corvette in Libya with sea drones
items.summary: President Zelenskyy confirmed Ukrainian naval drones launched from a mothership sank the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi port and hit a weapons cargo ship. The strike extends the war deep into the Mediterranean and Africa, far from the front lines. This shows Kyiv’s long-range reach and risks drawing more players into the conflict, keeping geopolitical uncertainty high for risk assets.
items.impact: widens war geography and raises escalation uncertainty

items.title: Iran claims mines hit three US-escorted tankers in Hormuz
items.summary: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards say three oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz despite US air escort, while Washington adds more sanctions on Iranian shadow banking. Oil still fell to three-month lows on rising supply and mediation talks involving Qatar and US officials. Energy shocks and blockade risks remain the key swing factor for inflation and risk appetite.
items.impact: oil volatility and Hormuz risk premium unresolved

items.title: EU unveils 22nd Russia sanctions package hitting banks
items.summary: The European Commission proposed cutting about 60 more Russian banks from SWIFT, cracking down on crypto and payment networks used for evasion, expanding energy repair bans, listing more shadow fleet tankers, and restricting Russian athletes and ex-soldiers. It still needs full member-state approval. Extra pressure on Russian finance and crypto routes matters for capital flows and any remaining sanctions-evasion activity.
items.impact: tightens Russian funding and crypto evasion channels

items.title: Pentagon delays Patriot interceptors for Ukraine
items.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has still not signed off on roughly 60 Patriot interceptors already paid for by allies, including some from European stocks. Ukraine faces continued Russian ballistic missile pressure with thin air-defense stocks. Delayed Western hardware raises the odds of more infrastructure damage and a longer, messier war that keeps risk assets on edge.
items.impact: weakens Ukraine defenses and prolongs conflict risk

items.title: South Korea air-raid alert after Russian jets approach
items.summary: Several Russian military aircraft entered South Korea’s air defense zone and came close to Ulleung Island airspace, triggering a brief civilian shelter alert and fighter scrambles. No territorial breach occurred but Seoul protested diplomatically. It fits a pattern of Russian probing of NATO and partner airspace that keeps alliance tensions elevated.
